title: A release leg sets its own TMPDIR on the leg host
body:
hv's ruling of 2026-11-11 (option 1 of kovacs-sysadm's three, devbin-vc's recommendation): a release leg sets its own TMPDIR.

On a Linux leg host, `/tmp` can be a small tmpfs. On kovacs it is systemd's tmp.mount at 50% of 3.3G RAM, 1.7G with usrquota, and an Intent release leg with a large Rust target filled it on the 3.3.0 cut. The stopgap was a hand-added `export TMPDIR="$HOME/tmp"` in kovacs's molt-generated `~/.config/molt/env.sh`, which Molt cannot render: its env liberator publishes a fixed set of variables and refuses values containing `$`.

Ask: the leg's far side (the `ssh host 'bash -s'` run in `lib/release.legs`) exports TMPDIR to a directory inside the leg's own per-run work area on the host's disk, makes it before the gates run, and clears it with the leg's worktree. Uniform for every project's leg, no per-project switch. Once it ships, kovacs's env.sh goes back to its render (kovacs-sysadm removes the hand line). Batched with 0333, the same leg code.
